newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU, Russia strike accord on steel trade.
newsitem.headline: EU, Russia strike accord on steel trade.

text.p: The European Commission said on Tuesday it had struck a deal with Moscow that will allow Russia gradually to increase its steel exports to the European Union to the end of 2001, when free trade will be introduced.

Under the accord, EU quotas on Russian steel will be raised for most products by 10 percent in 1997, to a total of 841,224 tonnes. They will increase a further five percent in 1998 and 2.5 percent more each year until the end of 2001.
The 1997 figure includes 430,000 tonnes of coils for rerolling, traditionally used by eastern German steel plant Ekostahl. That level will remain frozen until 1999.

The existing quotas apply to certain flat and long steel products from Russia and Ukraine representing less than 14 percent of the EU's iron and steel imports from those countries, the Commission said.
The EU reached a similar market-opening accord with Ukraine on March 20.
The deal with Russia adjusts the quotas to increase limits for coils and certain long products that Russia can export and cut others that it cannot fully use, the Commission said.

The timetable could be moved forward if Moscow applied competition, state aid and environmental disciplines compatible with those in the EU, the Commission said. The EU will provide technical assitance to help it do so, it added.
"Furthermore, the deal will be reviewed if Russia joins the (World Trade Organisation) before 2001," it added.

The accord, reached after negotiations in Moscow last week, will now be submitted to the EU Council of Ministers and the Russian government for approval, the Commission said. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
